speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (likely secondary to chronic scabies or other inflammatory dermatoses given the migration history, failed syphilis/eczema treatments, and significant smoking history).

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of the penile and digital lesions.
REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical photos of the lesions showing ulceration and induration.

Dr. Agent: Given the patient's history of unsuccessful treatments for syphilis and eczema, combined with the chronic non-healing nature of these lesions and significant smoking, I strongly suspect an underlying inflammatory trigger that has progressed to malignancy. We must confirm this with a biopsy immediately.
